newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bad weather halts Colombian bus crash rescue.
newsitem.headline: Bad weather halts Colombian bus crash rescue.

text.p: Bad weather halted the recovery on Monday of bodies from the wreck of a bus that plunged down an Andean ravine, killing 37 people.

The bus fell into the 1,500-foot (500-metre) deep canyon near the town of Ricaurte in southwest Colombian on Friday, killing its two drivers and 35 passengers -- almost all members of the same extended family.
A teenage girl, her uncle and a nine-month baby survived when they were thrown clear as the bus rolled down the ravine.
Red Cross officials said at least seven corpses were still trapped underneath the tangled wreckage of the bus.

"The weather has got much worse. Dense fog has closed in, the rain is torrential and the sides of the canyon are very slippery, making it almost impossible to climb down," Red Cross spokesman Mario Arias said.
The bus was on its way from Cali to the Pacific coast when it crashed. The driver had swerved to avoid a rockfall.
